source_a.title: Atelosteogenesis Type II: Pathophysiology, Genetics, and Skeletal Phenotypes

pairs.claim_a_text: The pathophysiology of AO2 is a failure of proper cartilage extracellular matrix sulfation.
pairs.claim_b_text: Biallelic pathogenic SLC26A2 variants reduce sulfate import into chondrocytes. This is the initiating molecular defect shared across the SLC26A2 chondrodysplasia spectrum.
pairs.rationale: Both concern the sulfation defect in AO2 (SLC26A2 disease), but A states the pathophysiology as failed matrix sulfation while B states the upstream cause (reduced sulfate import into chondrocytes) across the spectrum, so they are compatible and each adds a different step in the same mechanism.

pairs.claim_a_text: The pathophysiology of AO2 is a failure of proper cartilage extracellular matrix sulfation.
pairs.claim_b_text: Inadequate sulfate availability produces insufficiently sulfated proteoglycans and other cartilage-matrix macromolecules, compromising matrix composition and organization.
pairs.rationale: Both describe undersulfated cartilage matrix as the mechanism of atelosteogenesis type II (AO2), but B adds a specific cause (inadequate sulfate availability) and consequences (compromised matrix organization), while A states only the general sulfation failure, so neither is a clean subsumption nor identical.

pairs.claim_a_text: The pathophysiology of AO2 is a failure of proper cartilage extracellular matrix sulfation.
pairs.claim_b_text: Abnormal cartilage-matrix composition and organization impair the cartilage templates and growth-plate processes required for endochondral bone formation.
pairs.rationale: Both concern AO2 cartilage matrix defects, but A specifies a failure of ECM sulfation while B states a general matrix composition/organization abnormality impairing endochondral ossification; neither contains the other, and together they give cause and downstream consequence.

pairs.claim_a_text: The pathophysiology of AO2 is a failure of proper cartilage extracellular matrix sulfation.
pairs.claim_b_text: Disordered fetal cartilage growth and ossification generate severe limb shortening, characteristic hand and foot positioning, vertebral and long-bone abnormalities, and craniofacial malformations.
pairs.rationale: Both concern atelosteogenesis type II (AO2) and are compatible, but A gives the molecular pathophysiology (defective cartilage matrix sulfation) while B gives the clinical skeletal phenotype, so each adds something the other lacks.

pairs.claim_b_text: Small thoracic dimensions restrict fetal lung growth, while abnormal laryngeal, tracheal, and bronchial cartilage produces stenosis and dynamic airway collapse. Together these lesions explain the usual perinatal respiratory lethality.
pairs.rationale: Both concern atelosteogenesis type II (AO2) but A states a cartilage matrix sulfation defect as the underlying cause while B describes the thoracic and airway cartilage consequences leading to respiratory lethality; they are compatible and each adds something the other lacks, without stating the same fact.
